title: Artemis A: untuned Gemma 4 E4B-it, prompted, constrained JSON output
status_detail: Prepared on 2026-10-19 in Mission 001. Nothing was served or evaluated: there is no GPU on the preparation machine and no paid compute is authorised. Arm A needs no training and no train split.
hypothesis: Prompted with the evaluation runner's openai_compatible prompt and constrained to its 7-key JSON schema, untuned google/gemma-4-E4B-it matches the best deterministic baseline on text-only status_code detection and exceeds it on procedure detection for colloquial and non-ko/en questions, with zero parent-for-subcode substitutions and zero visa/stay scope mixes.
null_hypothesis: The untuned model does not beat the best deterministic baseline after cheap rule fixes on any text-only classification metric, or it introduces critical errors the rules do not make. Then Artemis is not needed for these tasks and the rules stay authoritative.

baselines.what: Production /api/ask contract: _detect_visa_codes + _detect_task_type + understand(), PYTHONHASHSEED pinned to 0.
baselines.known_limits: Discards every subcode from free text (R4) and is hash-seed nondeterministic without the pin (R2).
English article false positives ('a 3' -> A-3, R3), token glue ('D-10 to' -> D-10-TO, R6), multilingual procedure loss (R12).

baselines.what: The better of B1/B2 after the cheap rule fixes listed in 13-artemis-experiment.md §6 (hash-seed pin, article/number guard, token-boundary fix, Python subcode reading). Not built in Mission 001.
baselines.known_limits: Does not exist yet; the decision rule cannot be applied until it does.

base_model.params: 8.00B total, 4.5B effective; dense with per-layer embeddings; text, image and audio towers; 131,072 context
base_model.source: research-notes/models.md §3a (HF API, 2026-10-19, SHA re-checked by the verifier) and §5 Artemis rank 1
base_model.license_note: HF cardData says apache-2.0 and gated: false. No Gemma 4 repo ships a LICENSE file; archive Google's licence page beside the SHA (models.md §3a verifier note). Whether the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy binds Apache-2.0 Gemma 4 is unresolved (models.md §4, §8).
base_model.loader_note: The checkpoint class is Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration. Whether AutoModelForCausalLM loads it text-only is UNVERIFIED (models.md §8); the smoke step in training/README.md must confirm it or switch the loader.

secondary_model.note: Run the same arm on E2B only if E4B passes the safety gates; the smaller model is preferred when it scores within the CI of E4B (models.md §5 design note).

train.note: Arm A trains nothing. The train definition is listed so that A, B and C share one data definition. Benchmark v0 has no train split, so the train file does not exist.

leakage_guard.why: Template siblings that differ in one status code share most word 3-grams (about 0.6 Jaccard for a six-token question, INFERRED); 0.5 refuses them, and the fix is a re-split by case template (training-distill.md §4.6), never a higher threshold.

scoring_rules: Text-only items only: input.payload_status_code is null, so a code passed as payload cannot be scored as detection (status-classifier.md §9 rule 4).
A subcode is scored only from the explicit subcode field; an output equal to the parent code is a wrong subcode, never a hit (status-classifier.md §9 rule 1).
Procedures are scored on the 16 fine ids and also mapped through contracts.FINE_TO_COARSE; items whose fine id has no coarse equivalent are reported as not scorable for backend baselines.

prompt.defined_in: waymaker_ai/evaluation/baselines/model.py (build_messages, system_prompt, DECODING) and waymaker_ai/evaluation/predictions.py (model_output_schema); sft_dataset.prompt_sha256 hashes all three
prompt.note: Training and evaluation use the runner's own openai_compatible request: one system prompt and one 7-key schema for both Artemis tasks, user message = question (prefixed by the UI payload code when present). A change to the runner's prompt, schema or decoding changes this hash and the config stops loading.

hardware.assumption: One 16-24 GB NVIDIA GPU (compute class C1, training-distill.md §2.0) for serving only.
fits: L4 24 GB: E4B in bf16 (about 16 GB of weights, INFERRED from 8.00B parameters) with vLLM.

T4 16 GB: no native bf16, so serve in fp16; E4B in 16-bit does not leave room for the KV cache, so use E2B in fp16 or a 4-bit E4B (official QAT GGUF with llama.cpp). Estimates from models.md §3b and §6, all INFERRED.

compute.note: Local GPU, free Colab T4 or Kaggle only. A rented GPU is a paid run and is not authorised in Mission 001.

cost.basis: Inference only. $0 on a local GPU, free Colab or Kaggle. If an owner later authorises a rental: 1-3 hours of one L4 at RunPod Secure $0.59/h is about $0.6-1.8. Hours are INFERRED for a benchmark of a few hundred short items.
sources: research-notes/cost.md §5: Colab free T4 (UNVERIFIED quota), Kaggle about 30 GPU-hours/week (UNVERIFIED)

evaluation.runner: waymaker_ai.evaluation (built by a sibling task in Mission 001; confirm its command-line flags with --help)
serving: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server at the pinned revision, with JSON-schema structured outputs (training-distill.md §2.2, constrained decoding).
llama.cpp llama-server with the official QAT GGUF when the GPU is a T4.

decoding.why: The runner's own setting. Labels, not prose: greedy decoding with a fixed seed makes a run repeatable. training-distill.md §4.2 fixes temperature 0.2 for answer wording, which Artemis does not produce.

evaluation.split_discipline: Prompt and decoding choices are made on dev only. test and adversarial_holdout are scored once per configuration, against a frozen hash manifest of the benchmark files.
metrics: subcode_exact (a parent in the subcode field or a parent fallback is wrong)
flags parent_fallback + parent_in_subcode_field (critical; CLE-4): count must be 0
procedure_coarse (via contracts.FINE_TO_COARSE; items with no coarse equivalent are reported as not scorable)
flag procedure_scope_mixed (critical; CLE-3: a visa-scope procedure for a stay question or the reverse): count must be 0
not_status_token_respected and flag code_from_non_code_token ('a 3 month' must not become A-3)
structured-output validity rate (answers with no schema violation)
per adversarial class and per language (ko, en, other) breakdown
evaluation.reporting: Point estimate with a 95% bootstrap CI per split; per-language breakdown (ko, en, other).

gates.condition: dev, test and adversarial_holdout are frozen with a committed hash manifest before the first scored run.
gates.source: training-distill.md §4.7 G0; 12-evaluation-methodology.md governs the benchmark freeze
gates.on_fail: Do not score test or adversarial_holdout.

gates.condition: The runner's flags parent_fallback, parent_in_subcode_field and procedure_scope_mixed occur 0 times on test and adversarial_holdout.
gates.source: training-distill.md §4.5 CLE-3/CLE-4 and §4.7 G1; CLAUDE.md code hierarchy and procedure scope rules; 12-evaluation-methodology.md critical-error definitions
gates.on_fail: NO-GO: the arm ends; the model may not be used even as a fallback.

gates.condition: Structured-output validity is 1.0 (no schema violation) under constrained decoding.
gates.on_fail: NO-GO until the serving stack enforces the schema.

gates.condition: Decision rule: a model arm is pursued only if B-fixed is below the dev targets in 12-evaluation-methodology.md on text-only subcode_exact or procedure_fine, and the model arm beats B-fixed there with a 95% CI that excludes 0.
gates.threshold: targets set in 12-evaluation-methodology.md; this config sets none of its own
gates.on_fail: Keep the deterministic classifiers; do not start arm B.

gates.condition: p95 latency fits inside the Quick Answer budget, so routing never consumes the whole timeout.
gates.threshold: p95 well under 7000 ms (the Quick Answer timeout, training-distill.md §4.7 G6); the exact routing budget comes from 12-evaluation-methodology.md
gates.on_fail: NO-GO for online use; offline use only.

limitations: No Korean-specific benchmark exists for Gemma 4 (models.md §3b: MMMLU only, VENDOR-REPORTED); this arm is the first Korean measurement.
The benchmark labels are synthetic or machine-checked; none is human-verified yet (05-legal-intelligence-architecture.md §3).
The benchmark directory path is assumed (datasets/benchmark/v0); align it with the benchmark task's output before the first run.
